title: Indie devs using AI for pixel art: what's your actual workflow?
author: Mobile-Scientist-696
selftext:
My tool is at [spritelab.dev](http://spritelab.dev) if anyone wants the full picture or would like to try it out.   
  
I'm mostly posting because I'm curious how others in this space are tackling similar problems:  
\- What's missing from current AI pixel art tools that you'd actually pay for?  
\- Multi-view (4 or 8 dir): AI generated, handmade, or hybrid?   
\- Animation pipelines: AI for motion, or still frame by frame in Aseprite?  
\- Background removal on AI sprites: solved problem now, or still painful?  
  
Trying to figure out what's solved vs what's still painful, partly to inform what I build next.

P.S. If you want some bonus free credits for my site, drop me a message :) thanks for reading.

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body:
I'll check it out!   
  
Do you happen to know how does it differ from AutoSprite and the others out there??

replies.author: Mobile-Scientist-696
replies.body:
Thanks! Let me know how you find it/if you'd like some bonus credits.  
My site is the only one with this amount of fine-tuning options enabled post-generation. AKA, even after generating you can resize, change the number of colours, etc. The animation pipeline and background removal is also distinct/not commonplace, so the outputs will differ compared to competitors.
